Subject: Sponsor playback + embed security for July 14 webinar

Hi Soojin —

Quick note ahead of next week's technical run. Our sponsor (Bright) is sending a 15s pre-roll spot that needs to be served only to registered attendees and should not be downloadable. They requested the clip be embedded via a tokenized playback URL (short-lived, single-use). Two questions:

1) Can ON24 host the pre-roll asset behind a signed URL / token that expires after first playback?
2) If we use Zoom for the live stream (simulcast to ON24 embed), can the embed tokenization be enforced for the ON24 embed frame specifically (we want to avoid a direct link being used to seed the clip on other pages)?

Also: we have a small subset of registrants (internal testing group) who need to preview the sponsor clip before the live date. Can we create an allowlist (emails) that bypasses the 1st-play restriction for test accounts?

Attached: sponsor_pre-roll.mp4 (watermarked master), and embed_spec_v2.pdf with our expected token format.

Thanks,

Thanks Samir — looping in ON24 and Zoom to confirm constraints and proposed plan. High-level ask from Acme / Bright: tokenized single-use playback for sponsor pre-roll when served inside the ON24 embed, plus an internal allowlist for QA. Our constraints:

- Live workflow is Zoom -> ON24 simulcast (Zoom RTMP to ON24). ON24 will serve the embed frame on customer pages.
- Sponsor clip must be non-downloadable (we're OK with visible watermark for this run).
- Token lifecycle: issue token at time of player initialization, token scope limited to session_id + embed_origin, expiry 5 mins after issuance; allowlist accounts get a long-lived test token.

Requests for ON24/Zoom:
1) ON24: can you host the asset in your CDN and accept an HMAC-signed query param for playback authorization? We need single-use semantics (invalidate token after first successful playback handshake).
2) ON24: can the token include the origin header check so the clip only plays inside the ON24 iframe served at redwood.com pages?
3) Zoom: any implications on the simulcast flow that would surface a direct asset URL when we RTMP ingest the sponsor clip? (We plan to stitch the clip server-side on ON24, not inject via Zoom.)

Marissa/Ben/Laureen — can you confirm we have legal signoff on the watermark and the allowlist emails (I included a proposed list in the Drive link)? Also want to confirm that the registrant preview list (10 people) will be given a pre-release link with extended token TTL.

Plan proposal:
- ON24 hosts sponsor_pre-roll.mp4 behind signed endpoint
- Redwood issues signed tokens via a small auth endpoint we maintain that ties token to session_id + timestamp
- ON24 validates token once, serves clip, then marks token as used in an ephemeral cache
- Allowlist tokens with longer expiry created for QA accounts

Thanks — appreciate quick confirmation so we can do an early test July 6.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Events Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Forwarding the vendor responses as they arrive — below my notes:

- Legal: watermark OK for paid sponsor assets; compliance wants a short log of who was allowed preview access. Make sure we capture that in the registrant audit.
- Product/Platform: We should avoid adding server state in ON24 for token invalidation if possible. Prefer an HMAC that includes a nonce stored by Redwood in a short-lived cache so we control invalidation (Redwood issues nonce -> ON24 validates HMAC and calls back to our validation endpoint). This minimizes vendor-side stateful changes.

Hi Soojin / Samir —

Thanks for the clear spec. ON24 can host the asset and validate an HMAC-signed token as described. A few implementation notes:

- We will accept an HMAC token parameter (hmac_token) that contains: session_id, origin, expiry_ts, nonce. We will validate HMAC using the shared secret and then call your validation endpoint to ensure nonce hasn't been used.
- Single-use: ON24 will call back to your validation endpoint with the nonce and playback session_id immediately on first handshake. If your endpoint responds "valid", we mark token used and proceed. If you respond "invalid" we return 403.
- Origin enforcement: we will check the Origin header and the embed iframe referer; however, for some older browsers Referer may be absent. We recommend also passing embed_origin param to the HMAC payload to reduce false positives.
- Allowlist/test tokens: we can accept a query param test_preview=true; for these tokens we will skip single-use invalidation but still require HMAC validation. Please list preview emails and we will tie preview tokens to registrant_id for logging.

Operational items:
- We'll need the shared HMAC secret (we can provision a per-account key) and the Redwood validation endpoint URL (POST /token/validate) to be reachable from ON24.
- ON24 also needs the pre-roll MP4 accessible in our storage; you can upload to our secure bucket or we can pull from your signed URL for ingest. If you upload to ON24, we will provide a stream_key.txt (attached).

We can run the preview test July 6 at 09:00 PT — Ben, please share your dial-in for the test harness and we will load the pre-roll.

Regards,
ON24 Ops Team
